messages:
Priya: Quick sync 1 Sales pushed a list of bespoke pricing packs tied to old SKUs. They want a migration path to our 2025 standardized tiers before quarter-end. We need scope, constraints, and launch gates.
Ethan: Important to separate legal guarantees from commercial niceties. Which customers actually have SLA language vs informal commitments?
Lena: Ill run a contract grep for keywords: "service level", "priority capacity", "burst credits", "guaranteed throughput" and surface results.
Noah: Product-level constraint: supporting dual enforcement (legacy vs new) will mean extra routing logic + billing mapping. Ops will need a safe rollback.
GovBot: Heads up: any contract with explicit throughput numbers or "priority capacity" are binding. Changes require mutual amendment. Admin note: also check orders that reference an SOW with appendix B.
Priya: Proposal v1: 1) Classify customers: enforceable, negotiable, opt-in; 2) Offer 12-month grandfather window for enforceable items unless contract says otherwise; 3) Runtime flag + billing tag for legacy behavior; 4) Pilot then phased rollout.
Ethan: Who authorizes >12mo extensions? Recommend RevOps + Legal + CRO approval for >12mo. Sales can approve up to 3 months with RevOps sign-off.
Lena: Deliverable: list of affected contracts + redlines per account by Fri. Ill also tag clauses with "must preserve" vs "can change with notice."
Noah: Technical design outline: add a per-tenant field legacy_tier_profile. Serving control plane consults mapper service: if legacy profile present => apply caps, route priority labels, and emit billing_tag=legacy. If absent => normal path. Pseudocode: 
```
profile = tenant.legacy_tier_profile
if profile:
  apply_caps(profile.caps)
  set_routing_priority(profile.priority)
  add_billing_tag("legacy")
else:
  normal_flow()
```
Noah: Also need a fallback: if strict priority path exhausted, rules allow fallback to compatible variants but must log incident + require manual review for SLA-preserved tenants.
Priya: Launch criteria checklist: (A) Legal decision memo, (B) Sales playbook + customer comms, (C) runtime feature flag + mapper implemented and QA'd, (D) telemetry schema added, (E) pilot of 4 accounts completes with no SLA regressions.
Ethan: Telemetry needs: tenant_id, legacy_profile_id, migration_notification_ts, effective_sla_label, routing_fallback boolean, billing_tag. Make sure PII-free.
Lena: RevOps question: if customer moves from legacy expensive tier to cheaper new tier mid-window, do we auto-credit or require negotiation? Finance historically negotiates credits case-by-case. Product should surface impact but not assume credits.
Priya: Agreed. Add credits decision to launch gates (Finance OK).
Noah: Effort estimate: mapper + flag + simple billing tag plumbing = 2 sprints. E2E tests + dashboard filters = 1 sprint. Pilot support + rollouts = part of next sprint. Worst-case incident risk: medium.
Tara: Ops note: dashboards will need a per-tenant filter and an alert that fires if SLA-preserved tenants experience >2x latency or >5% error spike post-migration.
Priya: Pilot plan: pick 4 accounts across patterns (reserved-heavy, bursty, steady small requests, mixed). Sam from Sales to secure opt-in for pilot. Rollback plan = flip legacy_tier_profile flag off/on + re-run any billing reconciliation.
Ethan: I'll draft the policy doc and escalation matrix. Legal, please add mandatory language examples we must honor.
Lena: I'll upload contract hits to the shared drive and mark high-risk customers.
Noah: I'll post an eng RFC with mapper API + rollout steps by Thursday.
Tara: Ill add dashboards/alerts work item and a short runbook for rollback.
Priya: Action items recap: Lena - contract grep and list; Sam - pilot outreach; Noah - RFC + impl ETA; Ethan - policy doc + approval matrix; Tara - observability + alert; Finance/RevOps - credit policy decision. Sync Thursday for signoffs.
